title: Googling "Zelda" today offers a glimpse of how search worked in 1998
gist: Google added a Zelda Easter egg that reverts search results to a 1998-style list of blue links to hype Nintendo's Ocarina of Time remaster for Switch 2 (launching Nov 5 at $60/$70). Ars uses it to note how much Google search has shifted toward AI, sponsored content and social links that many users dislike.

insights.claim: Today's Google search results push web links far down the page beneath AI, sponsored content, suggested searches, and social media links.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Organic web traffic from Google is structurally squeezed by AI and ads.
insights.locator: You can go back to the modern

insights.claim: Google's push into generative AI is transforming search in a way that many people don't like, and the retro Easter egg highlights how far the core product has drifted from its minimalist roots.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: User dissatisfaction with AI-heavy search is a latent competitive vulnerability for Google.
insights.quote: Google’s push into generative AI is transforming search in a way that many people don’t like.
insights.locator: The Ocarina of Time left its mark

insights.claim: Classic Google showed 10 links per page; the Easter egg shows a curated list of seven links rather than a real search.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Nostalgic marketing, not a product option.

insights.claim: Google's Zelda Easter egg likely aims to leverage nostalgia to build hype for Nintendo's Ocarina of Time remaster launch.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Cross-brand nostalgia marketing between Google and Nintendo.
insights.locator: The Ocarina of Time left its mark

insights.claim: The Ocarina of Time remaster is a full re-creation for Nintendo Switch 2 with modern controls, priced at $60 digital and $70 physical, launching November 5.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Nintendo continues premium pricing for remastered back catalog on Switch 2.
insights.quote: The game is available for preorder now at $60 for digital and $70 for physical.
insights.locator: The Ocarina of Time has changed
